name: One-bit dither
one_line: Two colours only; every shade is made of dots.
look_words: Everything in two colours: a warm off-white and a near-black. There is no grey; every in-between shade is a pattern of dots, so a wall in shadow is a dense stipple and a sky is a sparse one. Shapes need strong silhouettes and clear light and dark sides, because colour cannot help. What matters is marked by brightness and shape instead: pickups are solid white and blink, hazards are solid black with a jagged edge, the player is solid white with a black outline. Light is one hard source. Motion is crisp, and the dot patterns stay fixed to the world so they do not crawl. Avoid fine detail, soft gradients, thin text and any third colour.

palette.name: one-bit
palette.notes: These are greys on purpose: a dither look turns each grey into a dot pattern of the two colours, so the roles differ by brightness. Without the dither look installed the game is plain greyscale. Player and pickups are both white: tell them apart by shape and movement.

upgrade.why: a small exact-palette render is the right base for a two-colour dither

music.mood: a single reedy organ or accordion line
music.notes: One voice, like a one-bit speaker.

sound_feel: clicks, ticks and short beeps; nothing lush
